decision: pending permissions are a FIFO list, not a single slot
why: an agent can request permissions for parallel tool calls; a single slot would lose one

decision: stop keeps the clb/<id> branch and deletes only the worktree directory
why: commits the agent made survive stop; only uncommitted changes are discarded

decision: stop on a failed run keeps the failed state and only retries worktree cleanup
why: overwriting failed with stopped hides why the run ended; repeating stop must converge
evidence: lifecycle_test.go stop on a failed run keeps the failure

decision: skip the architect arena for this design

decision: no store interface in the daemon; tests use the real SQLite store

decision: split the build into three workers on separate worktrees: adapters, backends with the fake agent, and daemon with ipc, cli, and E2E

why: the daemon actor and session cleanup are the subtlest concurrency in the project; the adapters are routine

decision: session generation counter in the daemon actor
why: after stop, finish, and a resumed follow-up, a late TurnEnded from the old agent process must not end the new turn; the lifecycle alone cannot tell old from new

decision: a graceful shutdown leaves active runs active in the store, and the next start fails them with 'daemon restarted while the run was active'
why: the agent's turn state after a restart is unknown, so resuming could repeat or skip work; failing is honest and fires the webhook
result: a run active at shutdown cannot be continued; launch a new run

decision: after the 10s close wait the daemon removes the worktree or resumes even if Close has not returned
why: Close is bounded by proc.Stop, which sends SIGKILL after its grace period, so the wait expires only for a process that SIGKILL cannot end; blocking forever would wedge the run
result: logged as a warning when it happens

decision: print mode treats a missing result line as failure, forwards non-JSON stdout as stdout events, and builds the summary from the text parts of assistant lines
why: a turn without a result line cannot be told apart from a crash; dropping stray output would hide CLI warnings; assistant lines are assumed to be whole messages
evidence: stream.go Prompt and parseLine; stream tests
result: open item 6: line shapes unverified on the real CLI

decision: fixed three README statements the code contradicted: finished does not mean the process has exited, replayed history is not stored again, and an existing ~/.clb keeps its mode
why: cross-model review
evidence: README.md How it works, Lifecycle, Security

decision: kept row 21's flake rates as the backends worker's numbers
why: the row already says 'per worker'; rerunning 80 stress iterations adds no decision

decision: row 23 was wrong: a session flooding events made stop take the full 10s close wait; posts from a session now give up once its generation is closed
why: cross-model review challenged the bound; a test with a flooding session reproduced it at 10.13s with the close-wait warning
result: red at 10.13s, green at 1.2s; daemon suite 20 of 20 under -race

decision: approve and deny select only allow-once or reject-once, and reply cancelled when the agent offers neither
why: the old fallback selected allow-always, a standing rule that lets the agent skip later approvals and breaks 'nothing is approved by default'
result: red on both fallback cases, then green

decision: merged the comment pass, then restored the comments that state constraints: run ownership, the shutdown-proof write context, worktree creation on the run goroutine, permission ID numbering, the close wait, and migration counting
why: the pass deleted 131 lines and about a dozen carried reasons the code cannot show, including the reason for the shutdown fix

decision: took two of the comment pass's eight refactors: the stale-generation check moved into postFrom, and exitGrace derived from proc.StderrWait
why: both remove a constraint that only a comment enforced; the guard move was mutation-checked and still fails 3 tests in 3 of 3 runs

decision: declined the other six: Serve running Recover, a row-plus-event store transaction, renaming runCall, routing rewriteLog through an actor, and a separate actor state struct
why: each restructures working code without fixing a failure; rewriteLog through an actor would start a goroutine for every finished run at startup; the listen-then-recover order has one caller and a comment

decision: c59af19 put four restored comments inside function bodies; 2b985cc removes those copies
why: zero-context patches applied at stale offsets, and the build cannot catch a misplaced comment; I now check that each top-level comment sits on a declaration

decision: trustWorktree opt-in passes --trust to agent -p; with it off, launch and followup on a print run fail with invalid
why: owner decision; --force, --yolo, and -f also pass the trust prompt but allow commands; failing at the request means no run or worktree is created

decision: end escaped descendants by an exact CLB_PROC_TOKEN entry in their environment, not by working directory
why: the owner's leaked shell had PPID 1 and its own group; a user's shell can sit in a run's worktree, so cwd matching can kill it
evidence: TestStopEndsDescendantsThatLeftTheGroup and its bystander and other-Process controls; e2e step a finished run leaves no background command running
result: shipped 46f37ea; darwin path runs only in CI

decision: keep the first 8 KiB of stderr and put the first 512 bytes in error
why: CLI errors lead with the message; the old tail capture lost it once stderr passed 8 KiB

decision: an agent that exits mid-request reads agent acp exited (status) before it answered <op>
why: the old <op>: prefix made a bad --model read as a login failure
evidence: TestStartReportsAnAgentThatExitsBeforeAnswering; binary run with --model invalid-model gave a 617-byte error

decision: summary is the turn's text blocks joined by newline; only tool_call and tool_call_update end a block
why: owner asked for blocks split by tool calls; thought chunks and command updates can arrive inside one message

decision: forward permission options as the agent sent them, with no computed approve or deny fields
why: the allow_once and reject_once rule lives in acp.go and the README; a second copy would drift
evidence: TestRequestPermissionForwardsOptions, TestPermissionOptionsRoundTrip; clb status on the binary

decision: skip print-mode thinking with the same unstoredEvents table
why: the owner saw thinking delta and completed lines from agent -p; both backends should store the same kinds

decision: leave ~/.cursor/projects folders and unknown print resume IDs to the CLI and document them
why: the folders hold the CLI's own chat data; clb cannot see that agent -p replaced an unknown chat
evidence: owner's manual tests on Cursor CLI 2026.09.18

decision: also end this user's processes whose working directory is inside the run's worktree, after the agent closes and before git worktree remove
why: owner decision after a retest: the CLI starts terminal commands with an empty environment, so CLB_PROC_TOKEN never reaches them; accepts that a user's shell in the worktree ends too
evidence: owner's ps eww and lsof on macOS; TestEndUnder cases and daemon sweep tests with mutations in bc-97f2ba8d report; binary run: an empty-env shell that traps SIGTERM in the worktree ended on clb stop, a sleep in the repo survived

decision: proc.EndUnder takes the directory from the daemon; proc.Stop still sweeps by token only
why: the daemon is the part that knows a directory is a disposable run worktree; a future caller could pass $HOME as cmd.Dir
evidence: mutation: Stop also calling EndUnder(cmd.Dir) fails proc_test.go:68 and :72

decision: read another process's cwd on macOS with the proc_info syscall, PROC_PIDVNODEPATHINFO
why: no cgo in this module, and lsof would add a subprocess per sweep; darwin/arm64 Syscall6 traps directly, with no variadic libc call
evidence: asm_darwin_arm64.s; macOS CI job runs the proc and daemon tests
result: shipped db0698e; staticcheck SA1019 suppressed with a reason

decision: raise closeWait from 10s to 15s
why: the worst case is about 8.2s for Close plus about 3.15s for one sweep
evidence: bc-97f2ba8d timing: 51ms for a sweep whose target dies on SIGTERM, 1.061s when it ignores SIGTERM

decision: sweep root: refuse a relative or symlinked worktree path and resolve only its parent with EvalSymlinks, then join the base name
why: EvalSymlinks on the whole path follows a worktree symlinked to $HOME and ends every process under it; resolving the parent still matches /private/var cwds on macOS when the dir is gone

decision: launch rejects a ref that starts with '-', resolves it with rev-parse --verify --quiet --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}, and Add passes the hash to worktree add
why: worktree add parsed a ref such as --detach or -q as a flag; update-ref accepts refs/heads/-q, so Add needs the hash even when launch checks
evidence: TestLaunchRejectsARefThatStartsWithADash, TestLaunchRejectsAnUnknownRef, TestAddRejectsABaseRefThatIsNotACommit, TestAddStartsAtABaseRefThatLooksLikeAFlag (red when Add passes baseRef); binary: --ref --detach and an unknown ref fail with invalid

decision: Recover ends the processes whose cwd is in each active run's worktree before it fails the run
why: the agent and its commands run in their own process group and session, so they outlive a daemon SIGKILL and keep editing a failed run
evidence: TestRecoverEndsProcessesLeftInAnActiveRunsWorktree (red with cb388a4 reversed); binary: an empty-env setsid sleep in the worktree survived restart on 85e8433 and ended on the fix

decision: only the newest generation sweeps the worktree after Close; sweepMu also makes startBackend wait for a sweep in progress
why: after an awaitClosed timeout the old goroutine's sweep ended the agent that the follow-up had just started
evidence: TestALateSweepSparesTheSessionThatReplacedIt; red when the sweeper check is dropped
result: shipped ff77bd2; closeWait became a var for the test

decision: clb stop commits uncommitted changes, untracked included and ignored excluded, to the run's branch before worktree remove --force; no hooks or signing; clb <clb@localhost> only when user.name or user.email is unset
why: refusing would strand a stopped run whose agent left edits; the branch already is where the user reviews the run's work
evidence: TestRemoveSavesUncommittedWork, TestRemoveSavesWhenGitIdentityIsUnset, TestRemoveLeavesTheWorktreeWhenTheSaveFails; e2e stop step; binary: dirty.txt landed on clb/<id> with the save message

decision: Add runs git worktree prune before worktree add
why: a worktree directory deleted by hand stays registered, so the follow-up's Add failed with 'already registered'
evidence: TestAddRecreatesADeletedWorktree (red with b3387e9 reversed); binary: follow-up after rm -rf of the worktree resumed

decision: UpdateRun stores the row and its status event in one transaction and returns the stored events for the NDJSON log
why: logs --follow could read the terminal row before the status event existed and exit without the final status line
evidence: TestUpdateRunCommitsTheRowAndItsEventsTogether, TestAFollowerThatSeesTheRunEndHasItsStatusLine (red when the event is appended after the row)

decision: Stop moves the run to a stopping state that is never stored; the removal's outcome, WorktreeRemoved or WorktreeRemoveFailed, is applied in the same job; removal runs under a.d.writes with a 1 minute timeout
why: a stop that raced shutdown cancelled its own removal, and a failed removal still stored stopped and fired a stopped webhook
evidence: TestAStopWhoseRemovalFailsFailsTheRun, TestAStopDuringShutdownStillRemovesTheWorktree, lifecycle table tests (red with b908a80 reversed); binary with index.lock held: exit 1, statuses queued running finished failed, webhooks finished failed, retry removed the worktree

decision: on macOS, Stop also ends the descendants a kqueue watch saw being born (EVFILT_PROC NOTE_FORK on each member, children listed with proc_listpids PROC_PPID_ONLY, membership by proc_info unique ID), plus the processes left in a group a member led when it exits; Linux keeps the token only
why: owner's macOS 26.6.2 Mac hides other processes' environments, so the CLB_PROC_TOKEN sweep found nothing; the watch does not read environments and has no OS-version check
evidence: probe runs 42384539807 and 42385038105: puniqueid resets to 1 on reparent, so a stop-time scan caught 0/60 orphans; 50ms and 250ms polling caught 0; kqueue caught 180/180 and 39/40; family-ci run 42387343828: empty, shell, node 30/30 per macOS runner with and without CPU load; red with the fix reverted and with watchFamily returning nil

decision: keep group adoption on member exit
why: a non-interactive shell's background job stays in the shell's group; the shell can exit before the watch lists its children
evidence: ablation in 42387343828: shell 19/30 per runner under load without adoption, 30/30 with it
result: accepted risk: an unrelated process could be adopted only if the group emptied and its exact pid was reused by a new group leader within the exit event's latency

decision: test hidden environments with an empty-environment grandchild and a node posix_spawn root instead of a seam
why: GitHub's macOS 15 and 26 runners have SIP off and show environments, so CI cannot hide them; the token is invisible to Stop either way
evidence: probe: ps -E shows CLB_X on macos-15 and macos-26 runners; node test skips without node
result: shipped in this commit; CI matrix names macos-15 and macos-26

decision: send webhook.headers on every delivery; webhook.CheckHeaders is the one list of names clb refuses: Content-Type, User-Agent, X-Clb-*, and also Host, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding
why: Grok Bot's routine trigger refuses a POST without the sender key; Go's HTTP client drops or rewrites Host, Content-Length, and Transfer-Encoding, so accepting them would send nothing and say nothing; two names that differ only in case would let map order pick the value
evidence: smoke on 401a4f6 with a receiver that wants Authorization: Bearer: answered 401, run log delivered false, and a headers field fails as unknown; TestSendExtraHeaders, TestCheckHeaders, e2e Authorization assertion
result: shipped; removing the copy in post fails TestSendExtraHeaders and the e2e step

decision: refuse, not warn, a config.json that sets webhook.secret or webhook.headers when its mode has any 0o077 bit
why: config.Load has no output channel, so a warning needs a logger in every command, and an assistant that parses stdout would not see it; OpenSSH refuses a loose private key the same way; the README already asked for chmod 600; group or other write lets a user repoint webhook.url and collect the key
evidence: TestLoadRefusesLooseWebhookFile covers 0644, 0640, 0620, 0604 with a secret, 0640 with headers, and 0600 and a plain 0644 file that still load
result: shipped; dropping the check fails the five loose-mode cases

decision: add no command that writes config.json; the existing 0700 home and 0600 files already meet the creation rule
why: clb never creates config.json, and the daemon already creates the home with MkdirAll 0700; a config writer would be new scope
evidence: smoke: a daemon started on a missing home created it 0700
